text:
incident-bot: ALERT: steady increase in KV cache paging on us-west-2; tail latency spike across continuous-batcher pools. svc:infra/kv-cache, metric:page_faults/sec, +420% in last 5m :rotating_light:

matt (oncall): i'm seeing the same in grafana, started ~08:23 UTC, paging correlates with large batched requests from chat-service.

kevin (eng-runtime): thanks, i'm on it. first thought: block manager eviction not keeping up -> metadata growth. pulling logs.

sara (eng-ml): any specific model or workload? could be a change in recent batching defaults that increased prefix sizes.

matt (oncall): looks like continuous-batching window increased for a canary rollout at 07:50. patch: `batching.window_ms=50->150` (canary). maybe causing larger KV block allocations.

kevin (eng-runtime): that matches. bigger windows -> larger sequence lengths -> more KV entries -> block fragmentation. trying to reproduce on staging now.

alex (eng-sre): customer impact report? are we serving 5xxs or just latency?

jade (customer-success): a few customers reported errors: two downstream services got timeouts ~08:27-08:35, one enterprise (org-id: org_892) hit 504s during heavy inference. they flagged it.

matt (oncall): mitigation plan I propose: 1) rollback canary batching.window to 50ms, 2) temp increase eviction aggressiveness (evict_threshold -> 0.6), 3) restart a subset of runtime pods to free leaked metadata.

kevin (eng-runtime): agree. I'll prepare a hotfix config and deploy as a targeted feature-flag rollback to canary nodes.

deploy-bot: STARTING ROLLBACK: rolling back feature flag `cb-window-canary` on cluster us-west-2 to 50ms (targets: runtime-canary-*) by kevin (eng-runtime).

matt (oncall): jade, can you notify org_892 that we're mitigating and may see brief retries? include ATTEMPTED mitigation.

jade (customer-success): on it. pinged account team and customer with ETA ~10m. said they'll hold non-critical spikes.

kevin (eng-runtime): quick note: looks like block metadata leak when block split happens under heavy append; the block manager's `meta_ref` count isn't dropping on some code paths. adding a guard now. patch ready for roll-forward if rollback insufficient.

sara (eng-ml): while kevin patches, can we also throttle continuous batching per-client for a quick fix? rate-limit large sequence aggregation.

kevin (eng-runtime): yes, toggling `max_agg_tokens_per_client=8000->2000` on canary. applying to 10% of nodes first.

deploy-bot: APPLYING CONFIG: `max_agg_tokens_per_client=2000` to runtime-canary-1..3.

kevin (eng-runtime): logs from canary node after config change (tail):
```
2026-03-15T08:33:12Z runtime[pid=3124] INFO KVBlockManager: split_block id=0x7f8a3 size=1.2MB
2026-03-15T08:33:13Z runtime[pid=3124] WARN KVBlockManager: meta_ref_count mismatch detected id=0x7f8a3 expected=0 got=1
2026-03-15T08:33:14Z runtime[pid=3124] INFO GarbageCollector: reclaimed 1.2MB metadata id=0x7f8a3
```

kevin (eng-runtime): after throttling, page_faults/sec dropping ~45% within 2m on canary. good sign.

matt (oncall): rollout status?

deploy-bot: ROLLBACK COMPLETE: feature flag `cb-window-canary` rolled back on runtime-canary-* (3 nodes).

kevin (eng-runtime): rolling eviction tweak next. will bump `evict_threshold` to 0.55 globally for affected pools, then monitor. this should reduce resident set and free stale KV blocks faster.

alex (eng-sre): do we have a quick script to restart only nodes with high meta_ref counts? i'd rather not restart everything.

kevin (eng-runtime): yes, running `scripts/evict_restart.sh --threshold 10000` to recycle nodes with meta bytes >10MB. kicking off now for us-west-2 pool.

matt (oncall): customer impact: jade, can you check if org_892's errors subsided after canary throttle/rollback?

jade (customer-success): customer reports latency back to normal and 504s stopped at ~08:40. they said they saw a few retries but overall working. will keep monitoring.

sara (eng-ml): we should add a guard in continuous-batching to reject single-request aggregations that produce >X tokens; keeps a noisy client from blowing caches. filing a ticket.

kevin (eng-runtime): patch queued: `guard-max-single-agg-tokens=12000`. also a fix for meta_ref decrement on block split in PR#4512. planning hotfix merge after post-mortem triage.

matt (oncall): status update to execs? short blurb: "paging spike due to batching canary -> rollback and throttling mitigated impact; hotfix for block manager metadata leak in progress; one enterprise customer experienced transient 504s, recovered." anyone object?

jade (customer-success): fine from CS side. they want a follow-up postmortem and ETA for hotfix.

kevin (eng-runtime): will prepare a postmortem draft and link PRs. ETA for production-safe hotfix (QA + canary) ~4-6 hours.

alex (eng-sre): I'll leave monitoring alerts muted for the related paging noise once metrics stabilize to avoid noise. document the muted alert IDs.

matt (oncall): ok team, handing over to kevin for follow-up and hotfix. I'm done with primary mitigation. kevin, you're on-call for the next hour for this incident, please run handoff when stabilizing.

kevin (eng-runtime): ack. thanks everyone. I'll add troubleshooting notes and follow-up actions to the incident doc.

matt (oncall): closing incident channel for now — will reopen if paging reappears. :white_check_mark:
